title: Acupuncture
what: The doctor places thin sterile needles at certain points on your body for a while.
why: Most often for chronic back or neck pain and headaches, as an add-on to your main treatment.
duration: a session usually takes 30 to 45 minutes, with needles in for 20 to 30 minutes; the doctor decides on the course
tell_doctor: If you have fainted from needles before
Skin conditions in the treated area

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not come hungry, but not right after a big meal either.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear loose clothes so the needed areas can be uncovered.

prepare.title: Needles
prepare.text: Needles should be single-use and sterile, opened in front of you.

bring: Your referral or doctor's report, if you have one
steps: Thin needles are inserted, quickly and not deep
You lie still with the needles in for 20 to 30 minutes
The doctor removes the needles and throws them away
feel: A quick light prick, often barely felt
Sometimes heaviness, warmth, or a dull ache near a needle
You may feel relaxed and sleepy
after: Sit for a few minutes before leaving
A small drop of blood or a bruise can happen and goes away on its own
red_flags: Severe weakness, fainting, or chest pain after a session: tell the doctor. With severe shortness of breath, call emergency services

faq.a: Usually not. The needles are very thin, and the prick is barely felt.

faq.q: Can I get an infection from the needles?
faq.a: No, if the needles are single-use and sterile. Ask for the pack to be opened in front of you.

reminders.text: Acupuncture today. Have a snack beforehand and wear loose clothes.
